content.title: Trump official rumored to be having affair grilled about jet bedroom, $220 million ICE ads
content.text: PoliticsHomeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem appears for an oversight hearing before the Senate Judiciary Committee, at the Capitol in Washington, Tuesday, March 3, 2026. (AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite)APBy Howard Koplowitz | hkoplowitz@al.comHomeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem defended her agency’s use of a luxury jet with a bedroom in it and spending $220 million on ICE ads featuring her as she faced a bipartisan grilling Tuesday during a Senate oversight hearing.Noem, who has been rumored to be having an affair with close adviser and former Trump campaign manager Corey Lewandowski, was confronted with a picture of the DHS jet by Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., during the hearing. Noem and Lewandowski, who are both married, have denied the reports.“These photos are not accurate. If you’re referring to the airplanes that the Department of Homeland Security has purchased, and are purchasing, we’re using them for long-range command and control aircraft that is dictated by statute in Congress for the Department of Homeland Security,” Noem testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee.“You did not use a luxury jet with a bedroom in it?” Whitehouse asked.Noem claimed the jet saves taxpayer money.“We used a 737. I’ve been on it once. But it is being used by other administration officials, and it is used for command-and-control flights for the department. The department has found that in purchasing our aircraft that we will save the taxpayers hundreds of millions of dollars,” she said.“Does it have a bedroom in it?” Whitehouse asked.“I believe it’s being refurbished and not having a bedroom in it, so it is being refurbished,” Noem responded.The senator was skeptical.“What kind of deportee justifies being flown out of the country in a luxury jet with a bedroom and accommodations like this?” Noem said, adding that the jet is used for “executive air travel and deportations.”Noem was also challenged by a Republican senator on her agency spending $200 million on advertisements that showcase her.“How do you square that concern for waste, which I share, with the fact that you have spent $220 million running television advertisements that feature you prominently?” asked Sen. John Kennedy, R-La.Noem defended the impact of the ads, which she claimed were approved by President Donald Trump.“Sir, the president tasked me with getting the message out to the country and to other countries where we were seeing the invasion come from, with putting commercials out that told them that if they were in this country illegally that they needed to leave or we would detain them and remove them and they’d not get the chance to come back to America the right way. That has been extremely effective,” she said.Noem said the contract for the ads were selected in a competitive bidding process and that career DHS officials chose the vendor.She denied Kennedy’s claim that the bid’s winners were people who did political work for Noem when she was an elected official in South Dakota.As to the ads effectiveness, Kennedy responded: “Well, they were effective in your name recognition. To me, it puts the president in a terribly awkward spot.”The Louisiana senator said he found it “hard to believe” Trump would have agreed to the ads.“I don’t think Russ Vought at OMB would’ve agreed to that,” Kennedy said, referring to the Office of Management and Budget director who has been tasked with cutting government spending. “It’s something we have to defend – I’m on the Appropriations Committee.“My research shows that you did not bid them out,” Kennedy said. “In fact, one of the people you picked – Safe America Media – was a company formed 11 days before you picked them. And that The Strategy Group got most of the money. The head of that is married to your former spokesperson.“Look, we all have friends who are qualified. I’m not quibbling with that,” Kennedy continued, adding that the contract “troubles me. “A fifth to a quarter of a billion in taxpayer money when we’re scratching for every penny … I just can’t agree with that, Madam Secretary," he said.Howard Koplowitz is AL.com's Breaking & Trending Reporter for afternoons and nights.
